summary: Updates RFC 3777 to allow the announcement of open positions and the request for volunteers for the nominating committee before its chair is named by the Internet Society President. It is a Best Current Practice, replaced by RFC 7437.

eli5.summary: Before the team leader is picked, you can already tell people that spots are open and ask for volunteers.

questions: how does the ietf pick leaders
who volunteers for the nominating committee
subtitle: Announce open positions before the committee chair is named

tldr.problem: The NomCom selection process required the chair to be named before positions could be announced, and a mandatory 30-day solicitation meant any delay in naming the chair pushed back the entire process.
tldr.mechanism: The IETF Executive Director can now issue the announcement of open positions and call for volunteers before the chair is named, allowing the search for a chair and recruitment of volunteers to proceed in parallel.
tldr.outcome: The NomCom chair can begin work immediately upon being named and effectively use face-to-face time at IETF meetings for interviews.

today: RFC 5633 is a Best Current Practice that updates RFC 3777. It was later superseded by RFC 7437.

sections.title: The NomCom and the Timing Problem
sections.content:
The IETF uses a Nominating and Recall Committee (NomCom) to select members of the Internet Engineering Steering Group (IESG), the Internet Architecture Board (IAB), and the IETF Administrative Oversight Committee (IAOC). The NomCom process is defined in RFC 3777.

One part of the process had a built-in delay: the NomCom chair must announce open positions and request volunteers, and volunteers have 30 days to respond. Until the chair is named by the Internet Society President, no announcement can be made, so the 30-day clock does not start. If the chair is named close to an IETF meeting, the NomCom cannot conduct face-to-face interviews at that meeting.
sections.eli5: Picking a team leader was taking so long that there was no time to find team members or interview them at meetings.

sections.title: What Went Wrong in 2008-2009
sections.content:
In 2008-2009, the chair was named less than 30 days before the second IETF meeting of the year. The 30-day solicitation period meant NomCom could not complete its interviews at that meeting, so the committee had to use email and conference calls instead. This was less effective than face-to-face time.

The root cause was that two separate things—finding a chair and finding volunteers—happened sequentially when they could happen at the same time.
sections.eli5: The leader picked late, so there was no time for the group to meet in person at their regular meetings.

sections.title: The Fix
sections.content:
Four weeks after the first IETF meeting each year, the President either names an Incoming NomCom Chair, or directs the IETF Executive Director to issue the announcement of positions and call for volunteers on behalf of the future chair. The Executive Director collects responses and hands them to the chair when the chair is appointed.

The RFC also lets the chair (or outgoing chair during the search) request the IETF Secretariat to perform clerical tasks that do not require chair judgment, with appropriate notification to the community.
sections.eli5: Four weeks after the first meeting, either the leader is named or the staff starts taking volunteers in the leader's name. When the leader arrives, the volunteers are ready.

sections.title: Status
sections.content: This update to RFC 3777 allows the recruitment phase to start earlier, eliminating the serial delay that hampered the 2008-2009 cycle. The document is Best Current Practice and was later replaced by RFC 7437.
sections.eli5: This small change lets the process move faster, so the committee can be ready when it needs to be.

references.text: Galvin, J., "IAB and IESG Selection, Confirmation, and Recall Process: Operation of the Nominating and Recall Committees", BCP 10, RFC 3777, June 2004.
Dawkins, S., "IAB and IESG Selection, Confirmation, and Recall Process: Revision of the Nominating and Recall Committees Timeline", RFC 5078, October 2007.
